Tom Clancy's The Division: Broken Dawn

Alex Irvine's licensed Division novel follows April Kelleher and Division Agents across a post-outbreak research trail in the months between the first game and The Division 2.

Connectionnot applicable Continuitydivision transmedia Canon scopeofficial transmedia Verificationsource reviewed Reviewed2026-07-28

A bridge between the games

Broken Dawn is licensed Division transmedia rather than a game mission. Ubisoft positions it in the gap between the first game and The Division 2, so this archive labels its claims official transmedia and keeps its story scope distinct from player-campaign chronology. [1][2]

Research trail

The novel's source-specific route moves from New York toward a Midwest antiviral lead. It connects civilian survivor April Kelleher with Agents Aurelio Diaz and Ike Ronson, then opens a Washington intelligence handoff that later game readers can recognize without turning the novel into a substitute for game evidence. [1][2][3]

Claim ledger

Every factual statement below must retain at least one traceable source.

  1. confirmed

    Ubisoft describes Broken Dawn as an official Division novel set in the months between the first game and The Division 2, with a story separate from the game's player campaign. [1][2]

  2. confirmed

    Its published premise follows April Kelleher and Division Agents Aurelio Diaz and Ike Ronson through a Midwest lead involving a potential broad-spectrum antiviral. [1][2][3]
